examples.ko: 닭 가슴살은 다이어트할 때 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: Chicken breast is eaten a lot when people are on a diet.
I bought a pack of breast meat at the supermarket.
The breast meat was dry, so I poured sauce on it.
After working out, I ate a chicken breast salad.
I packed a lunch box with chicken breast and eggs.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 가슴살로 만든 요리가 맛있어요.
examples.en: This shop's dishes made with breast meat are delicious.

explain: 고기 부위 이름이라서 사람 몸에는 쓰지 않아요. '닭 가슴살', '닭 다리살'처럼 앞에 어떤 고기인지 붙여 말해요. 사람의 가슴은 그냥 '가슴'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the name of a cut of meat, so it is not used for the human body. People put the animal in front, like '닭 가슴살' or '닭 다리살'. For a person's chest you just say '가슴'.

examples.en: I ordered a burger and fries set.

examples.ko: 감자튀김에 소금을 조금 더 뿌려 주세요.
examples.en: Please sprinkle a little more salt on the fries.
The fries that just came out are still warm.
I dip my fries in ketchup.
One large fries, please.

examples.ko: 감자튀김 냄새가 나서 참을 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: I smelled French fries and couldn't resist.

explain: 메뉴에는 '프렌치프라이'라고 쓰기도 하고, 친구끼리는 줄여서 '감튀'라고도 해요. 봉지에 든 얇은 과자인 '감자칩'과는 달라요. 햄버거 가게에서는 '감자튀김'이 세트 메뉴 이름으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Menus sometimes write '프렌치프라이', and friends shorten it to '감튀'. It is different from 감자칩, the thin packaged snack. At burger shops 감자튀김 often appears as part of set menu names.

examples.en: I add black beans to the rice when I cook it.
I drink black soybean milk every morning.
My mom soaked black beans and made braised beans.

examples.ko: 검정콩은 하루 전에 물에 불려 두세요.
examples.en: Soak the black beans in water a day before.
The black beans made the rice color darker.
I bought a bag of black beans at the market.

explain: '검은콩'이라고도 해요. 밥에 넣어 먹거나, 조림이나 두유로 만들어 먹어요. '검정'은 색을 나타내는 명사예요.
explain_en: It is also called '검은콩'. People put it in rice, or make it into braised beans or soy milk. '검정' is a noun that refers to the color black.

examples.en: After work I ate gopchang (grilled intestines) with a friend.
Gopchang tastes rich and nutty when grilled.

examples.ko: 이 골목에는 오래된 곱창집이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: There are really many old gopchang restaurants in this alley.

examples.ko: 한국에 와서 곱창을 처음 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried gopchang for the first time after coming to Korea.
Two servings of gopchang and one fried rice, please.

examples.ko: 곱창은 부추와 같이 먹으면 느끼하지 않아요.
examples.en: Gopchang doesn't feel greasy when you eat it with chives.

explain: 곱창집 메뉴에는 곱창, 대창, 막창이 같이 있어서 부위로 골라요. 곱창은 속의 기름기 때문에 고소하고, 막창은 쫄깃한 편이에요. 구운 곱창을 먹고 나서 볶음밥으로 마무리하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: Gopchang restaurant menus list 곱창, 대창, and 막창 together, and you choose by the cut. 곱창 is rich because of the fat inside, while 막창 is chewier. Many people finish the meal with fried rice after the grilled gopchang.

examples.en: On a hot day, a cold lemonade is the best.
I ordered a glass of lemonade at the cafe.
Please put more ice in the lemonade.
The children sold lemonade in the yard.
This lemonade is too sweet.
I tried making lemonade from lemons at home.

explain: 레몬즙에 물과 설탕을 넣어 만든 음료예요. 카페 메뉴에서는 '레몬에이드'라고 적혀 있는 것도 자주 볼 수 있어요. 둘 다 비슷한 음료를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is a drink made with lemon juice, water and sugar. On cafe menus you will often see it written as '레몬에이드', and both names refer to a similar drink.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁은 마카로니 치즈를 만들 거예요.
examples.en: Tonight I'm going to make macaroni and cheese.

examples.ko: 마카로니를 삶을 때 소금을 조금 넣어요.
examples.en: When I boil macaroni, I add a little salt.
There is macaroni in the salad, so it's tasty.
The kids like macaroni soup.

examples.ko: 마카로니는 몇 분 정도 삶아야 해요?
examples.en: About how many minutes do I need to boil the macaroni?
I bought a bag of macaroni at the supermarket.

explain: 스파게티, 펜네처럼 파스타의 한 종류예요. 보통 '마카로니 샐러드', '마카로니 치즈'처럼 다른 음식 이름과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is one kind of pasta, like spaghetti or penne. It is usually used together with other dish names, as in '마카로니 샐러드' or '마카로니 치즈'.

examples.en: I ate the muk with soy sauce seasoning on top.
Soft muk is hard to pick up with chopsticks.
My mom made muk from scratch for us.

examples.ko: 시장에서 묵 한 모를 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought one block of muk at the market.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 시원한 묵 한 그릇이 최고예요.
examples.en: On a hot day, a bowl of cool muk is the best.
You slice muk thinly with a knife.

explain: '도토리묵', '메밀묵'처럼 앞에 재료 이름이 붙어요. '묵무침', '묵사발'처럼 요리 이름에도 들어가요. 오래됐다는 뜻의 '묵다'와는 소리만 비슷하고 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: The base ingredient goes in front, as in '도토리묵' (acorn jelly) and '메밀묵' (buckwheat jelly). It also appears in dish names such as '묵무침' (seasoned muk salad) and '묵사발' (muk in cold broth). It is a different word from the verb '묵다' (to be old, to stay somewhere), which only sounds similar.

examples.ko: 시험 공부하다가 출출해서 밤참으로 라면을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I got hungry studying for the exam, so I ate ramyeon as a midnight snack.
If I sleep after a late-night snack, my stomach feels uncomfortable.
A late-night snack is provided when working overtime, so it's okay.

examples.ko: 단원들은 천막 뒤에 둘러서서 밤참을 먹고 있었어요.
examples.en: The troupe members stood around behind the tent eating a midnight snack.

examples.ko: 밤참 생각이 나서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I keep thinking about a midnight snack and can't fall asleep.

examples.ko: 밤참은 가볍게 과일로 먹는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For a midnight snack, it's best to keep it light with fruit.

explain: '야식'과 비슷하게 밤늦게 먹는 간식이나 음식이에요. '밤참을 먹다, 챙기다, 내오다'처럼 써요. '밤참으로 ~을 먹다'처럼 무엇을 먹는지 같이 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: Like '야식', it is a snack or food eaten late at night. You say '밤참을 먹다/챙기다/내오다'. People often add what they ate, as in '밤참으로 ~을 먹다'.

examples.en: In the afternoon I had biscuits with tea.
The biscuits in the opened bag have gone soft.

examples.ko: 배고파하는 아이에게 비스킷 몇 개를 줬어요.
examples.en: I gave a few biscuits to the hungry child.
I bought a tin of biscuits as a gift.
Butter biscuits aren't sweet and taste rich and nutty.
If you dip a biscuit in milk, it gets soft.

explain: 한국에서 '비스킷'은 작고 단단하게 구운 과자를 말하고, 더 크고 부드러운 건 '쿠키', 얇고 짭짤한 건 '크래커'라고 불러요. 모두 '과자'라는 큰 이름 아래에 들어가요. 요즘은 '비스킷'보다 '쿠키'나 그냥 '과자'라고 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea 비스킷 is a small, firm baked snack. A larger, softer one is a 쿠키, and a thin, salty one is a 크래커. All of them fall under the big name 과자. These days people say '쿠키' or just '과자' more often than 비스킷.

en: wild greens; mountain greens; mountain herbs

examples.en: In spring people go to the mountains to pick wild greens.
I ordered wild-greens bibimbap for lunch.
These are wild greens that my grandmother picked herself.
We blanch wild greens and season them to eat.
The wild-greens side dishes at this restaurant are tasty.
These wild greens have a slightly bitter taste.

explain: '나물'은 무쳐 먹는 채소 반찬을 두루 말하고, '산나물'은 산에서 자라는 것을 말해요. 고사리, 취나물 같은 것이 대표적이에요. 밭에서 키운 나물과 구분해서 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: '나물' broadly means seasoned vegetable side dishes, and '산나물' are those that grow in the mountains, such as '고사리' (bracken) and '취나물'. It is used to tell them apart from greens grown in fields.

examples.en: Apricots are sweet and sour, so we eat them as jam too.
I bought ripe apricots at the market.
When the apricot blossoms bloom, spring has come.
I drink tea with an apricot scent.
The apricot isn't ripe yet, so it's sour.

examples.ko: 살구 두 개를 깨끗이 씻어서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I washed two apricots well and ate them.

explain: '살구색'은 연한 주황빛 살색을 말해요. 예전에 쓰던 '살색'이라는 말 대신 요즘은 '살구색'을 써요. 비슷하게 생긴 '매실'과는 다른 과일이에요.
explain_en: '살구색' is a light orange, skin-tone color. These days people use '살구색' instead of the older word '살색'. It is a different fruit from the similar-looking '매실' (green plum).

examples.ko: 김치를 담글 때 젓갈을 넣으면 감칠맛이 나요.
examples.en: Adding jeotgal when making kimchi gives it a rich savory taste.

examples.ko: 할머니가 직접 담근 젓갈이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The jeotgal my grandmother made herself tastes the best.
Jeotgal is salty, so eat just a little.

examples.ko: 젓갈 냄새가 강해서 처음에는 먹기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The smell of jeotgal was strong, so it was hard to eat at first.

examples.ko: 흰밥에 젓갈 하나만 있어도 밥이 잘 넘어가요.
examples.en: Even with just one kind of jeotgal, white rice goes down easily.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구는 젓갈이 들어간 김치를 처음 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: My foreign friend tried kimchi made with jeotgal for the first time.

explain: 새우, 멸치, 명란 같은 해산물을 소금에 절여 삭힌 음식이라서 '새우젓', '멸치젓'처럼 이름 뒤에 '-젓'이 붙기도 해요. 반찬으로 먹기도 하고 김치 양념에도 들어가요.
explain_en: It is seafood such as shrimp, anchovy or pollack roe salted and fermented, so specific kinds often end in '-젓', like '새우젓' and '멸치젓'. It is eaten as a side dish and also goes into kimchi seasoning.

examples.en: I squirt ketchup on my fried egg.
We ran out of ketchup, so I went to the supermarket.

examples.ko: 저기, 앞에 있는 케첩 좀 건네주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, please pass me the ketchup in front of you.
My kids like ketchup a lot.
You can make ketchup from tomatoes.
I dunked the french fries deep into the ketchup and ate them.

explain: '케찹'이라고 쓰는 사람도 많지만 표준 표기는 '케첩'이에요. '뿌리다', '찍다'와 같이 써요. 한국에서는 감자튀김, 핫도그, 오므라이스에 케첩을 자주 곁들여요.
explain_en: Many people write it '케찹', but the standard spelling is '케첩'. It pairs with '뿌리다' (squirt) and '찍다' (dip). In Korea ketchup commonly goes with french fries, corn dogs and omurice.

examples.en: On rainy days I think of pajeon.
I dip pajeon in spicy soy sauce.
On the weekend my mom pan-fried pajeon for me.
Excuse me, one seafood pajeon, please.

examples.ko: 프라이팬 위에서 파전이 노릇노릇 익고 있어요.
examples.en: The pajeon is cooking golden brown in the frying pan.

examples.ko: 파전 반죽에 오징어를 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better if you put squid in the pajeon batter.

explain: '부침개'는 기름에 부친 음식 전체이고, 파전은 그중 파가 들어간 것이에요. 동사는 '부치다'를 써서 '파전을 부치다'라고 해요. '붙이다'와 헷갈리지 마세요. 한국 사람들은 비 오는 날 기름 소리가 빗소리 같아서 파전을 먹는다고 말해요.
explain_en: 'Buchimgae' is the general word for pan-fried batter dishes, and pajeon is the kind with green onions. The verb is '부치다' (pan-fry), as in '파전을 부치다', not '붙이다' (stick). Koreans often say they crave pajeon on rainy days because the sizzling sounds like rain.
